filename: Knowledge-guided Machine Learning_ Current Trends and Future Prospects.pdf
title: Knowledge-guided Machine Learning: Current Trends and Future Prospects
processes: carbon and water cycles in agroecosystems
testbed_rationale: This paper is a broad review and perspective article synthesizing knowledge-guided machine learning methods, paradigms, and use cases in environmental science; it does not produce or distribute a distinct benchmark dataset.
pain_points: Limited coverage of data distributions and scarcity of labeled ground-truth observations in environmental systems leading black-box ML to fail out-of-distribution
Competing loss objectives and difficult optimization landscapes with poor local minima when incorporating scientific constraints
Model imperfections and bias in process-based physical models affecting synthetic pretraining datasets
Catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning when adapting models pretrained on simulations to observational targets
Excessive computational and financial costs of running large foundation models over long time horizons and broad regions
Disparate data scales, spatial/temporal resolutions, and quality making integration across complex environmental domains difficult
extraction_notes: This manuscript is an overview/survey paper (arXiv:2403.15989v2) outlining principles, taxonomies, methods, and environmental applications of Knowledge-Guided Machine Learning (KGML). No original experimental datasets or dedicated software repositories are introduced.
